requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Backends with explicit checkpoints (Bedrock)**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a two-request Bedrock Claude conversation. It covers a tool-call round and a reasoning turn.
- For every request it asserts the system array has exactly two entries: the system text, then a `cachePoint`.
- For every request it asserts the last message's final block is a `cachePoint`. It also asserts the whole body contains exactly two `cachePoint` occurrences, so there are no extra checkpoints.
- It asserts the second request, which follows a reasoning turn, still ends in a checkpoint.
- Checkpoints must not change content. The test runs the same conversation against a non-caching model (`fixture-uncached-model`), which gets no `cachePoint`. It then asserts that each cached request, after `without_cache_points` strips the checkpoint blocks, equals the corresponding plain request.
- "When the backend and model support caching" is covered in two places. The CLI test checks the non-caching model end to end. The unit test `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]` checks `bedrock_caches` for Claude, an inference-profile ARN, Nova, Llama (negative) and an unknown model (negative).
- The same unit test checks that `place_cache_checkpoints` sets only the cache option, by comparing the serialized request with an expected one. It also checks that checkpoints are requested after a reasoning turn.
- Ollama has no explicit checkpoints, so it falls outside the "backends that accept explicit checkpoints" clause.

**OpenAI**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` asserts the `instructions` (system prompt) are non-empty and identical across both requests. It asserts the `tools` arrays are identical across the requests.
- It asserts the second request's `input` begins with exactly the first request's input, then the `function_call` and `function_call_output` in order. That covers replay of prior content in its original order.
- The recursive `assert_no_checkpoints` checks every request body for `cachePoint`, `cache_control`, and `cache_point` or `cache_checkpoint` type blocks. That covers "MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks".

**Not assessed here**
- The system prompt being identical across assessments of a kind is the job of `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts`. The CLI test also carries a {test} reference to that requirement.

I found no obligation, boundary or failure case without a test and an assertion.

For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
requirement, example, citation review, site review, and a verifier of each of
those. A system prompt MUST be the same for every assessment of its kind, so
every placeholder whose value depends on the subject MUST be in the subject
message.
